alignments.note: Rule 17: head on the lexical verb; the auxiliary is discontinuous under rule 15 because the ASV recasts the clause as a question.

Rule 5: the projection carries no negator in this clause. The ASV turns the Greek statement into a rhetorical question and supplies *not*, which answers to no source token; rule 86's test finds nothing to license it. Folding it onto κρινεῖ remains defensible.
Rule 31: an article preceding the noun it governs takes the determiner along with the supplied relativizer, headed on *the*, discontinuously under rule 15; the modifier ἐκ φύσεως is verbless.
Head noun, left bare by rule 31.
Rule 31 with rule 53: a prepositional modifier has no verb, so the copula goes with the preposition.
Rules 86 and 74: the participle carries the subordination, so the supplied *if* and the supplied subject are helpers on it.

Corrected from an alignment to *who*. Rule 92: rule 31's verbless-modifier carve-out does not reach an expressed appositional predicate noun, so where the ASV recasts the phrase as a finite relative clause the article takes only the determiner written for it — here the indefinite *a*, which rule 92 aligns to an article in all eight such corpus units — and the noun carries the relativizer and copula. Rule 57 forbids handing a supplied determiner to a noun standing behind its own article.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause: the supplied determiner belongs to the noun.

Corrected: rule 92 gives the expressed appositional predicate noun the supplied relativizer *who* and the supplied copula *art* along with its own word, headed on the noun, discontinuously under rule 15. Rule 53's test decides it — an expressed predicate noun is a token left to carry the supplied words, whereas a prepositional phrase is not.
Rule 51's anarthrous clause with rule 21: the supplied determiner and the case preposition go with the noun.

review_notes: Corrected s011/s016: the accepted alignment gave *who* to τόν under rule 31's verbless-modifier carve-out, but rule 92 says in terms that the carve-out does not reach an expressed appositional predicate noun. παραβάτην is such a noun and takes *who … art … transgressor*; the article keeps only the supplied *a*.
t003 *not* is kept added: the projection carries no negative particle in this verse and rule 86's licensing test finds no token for it.
s003 is unaffected: its modifier ἐκ φύσεως is a prepositional phrase with no verb, so rule 31's precede clause gives the article the discontinuous *the … which*.
